deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is a passage of natural philosophy: Riemann's critical, systematic restatement of Fechner's thesis (from Zend-Avesta) that the Earth is ensouled. The previous page announced that he would set aside Fechner's method of analogy and use 'abstraction of general laws by induction and their confirmation in explaining nature'. This page sets up that inductive criterion.

(1) It continues the claim from p. 41 that thinking is a process inside ponderable matter. Riemann holds it evident from inner perception that thinking cannot be explained by spatial motions of matter. For argument's sake he concedes the abstract possibility of such an explanation.

(2) Purposiveness (Zweckmäßigkeit) is observed on Earth. The question is where to locate the thought-process (Denkprozess) that causes it.

(3) He distinguishes two kinds of purposes. Conditioned purposes occur in bounded times and places. For them a cause bounded in time and space must be sought. Unconditioned purposes are explained by an eternal Willing, not produced in any temporal process. This sentence is written twice, the second time as a reformulation.

(4) The only purposiveness whose cause we directly perceive is that of our own actions. It arises from willing ends and deliberating about means. A line breaks off ('Ju...' or 'In...').

(5) Criterion, in schematic form (the formalization is mine).
- Setting: a body B of ponderable matter in which a system S of continuing purpose-and-effect relations comes to closure.
- Hypothesis: a continuing unified thought-process in B may then be assumed to explain S.
- This is the most probable hypothesis if (i) S does not already close within proper parts of B, and (ii) there is no reason to seek its cause in a larger whole W of which B is a part.
- In effect, the seat of the soul is the minimal closed carrier of the purposive system.

(6) Application to humans, animals and plants. Part of their purposiveness, the individual purposive behaviour, is explained by a thought-process inside these bodies. Another part, the purposiveness of the organism's structure, is explained by a thought-process in a larger whole.

(7) Reasons are listed starting with: (1) the purposiveness of organic arrangements does not find its closure in the single organism. The next page continues this, and then argues that the larger whole is the Earth.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematics.

Philosophical gap: condition (ii), 'no reason to seek the cause in a larger whole', is not operationalized. The criterion relies on the unproved premise from p. 41 that all explanation of purposiveness must go through a thought-process.
Redundancy: the sentence on unconditioned purposes and eternal Willing appears twice. The second version is evidently a draft reformulation.

results.what: Inductive criterion for locating a unified thought-process (soul): the minimal material whole in which a system of purpose/effect relations closes. Applied to separate individual purposiveness from organic purposiveness, the latter ascribed to a larger whole (the Earth, following Fechner).
results.modern_name: Teleological argument for panpsychism / world-soul; a systems-closure criterion for the seat of mind
results.usually_credited_to: G. T. Fechner (Nanna 1848, Zend-Avesta 1851); Riemann's philosophical fragments were partly published by Weber/Dedekind in the Gesammelte Werke (1876) as 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts'

deep.surprise_reason: A purely philosophical page. Riemann's engagement with Fechner and Herbart is well known from the published philosophical fragments, and this page contains no mathematical content.
transcription_corrections: The line beginning 'Es ist hier nur von bedingten...' starts a separate paragraph. Its content is restated in the following paragraph ('Für alle bedingte ...'), so the passage is a draft followed by its rewrite.
The truncated word at the end of the paragraph on our own actions ('Ju...') may be 'In...' or the start of a struck/abandoned sentence; it cannot be read definitively.
'(bildet) ist' is an alternative wording written above the line, not consecutive text. The same applies to '(vollkommen)' and '(Erklärungsweise)'.
